npcs.name: Maren Hale
npcs.idle: Have you seen a young man with a lantern and more nerve than sense? No? Then never mind me.

npcs.name: Hob Tanner
npcs.idle: I'm just here. Minding my business. Like a sensible man.

npcs.name: Brother Eadric
npcs.idle: Walk softly. Mithra's faithful have not stopped praying down here - they have only stopped breathing.

npcs.name: Ysolde Marchant
npcs.idle: Mind the loom. Everything else in this house is already unravelling.

npcs.name: Gerrit the Woodcutter
npcs.idle: Keep your voice down. They sing at night, up the hill, and I'd sooner they didn't hear us.

npcs.name: Tamsin
npcs.idle: Grandad says faeries can't count past three. I can count to a hundred. That's why I'm in charge.

quests.title: What the Tomb Keeps
quests.offer:
Please - a moment. My brother Caddoc went off four nights ago with a lantern, a shovel and a map he swore was worth a fortune. He said he'd be back by market day. Market day was yesterday.

He's reckless, not stupid. Mostly. His friend [Hob] knows more than he lets on. Will you [look for him]? I'd go myself, but someone has to keep our mother from going after him.

topics.Hob: Hob Tanner. They go everywhere together - or did. Hob's been jumping at shadows since Caddoc left. He's by the east road, pretending to work.

quests.summary: Maren Hale's brother Caddoc went treasure hunting four nights ago and never came home.

steps.goal: Ask Hob Tanner where Caddoc went
steps.say: Maren sent you? Gods. All right. We bought the map off a pedlar in Ludlow - an old Mithran thing, he said, from the tomb in the eastern hills. Caddoc was set on it. I went with him as far as the [barrows] and then I... I came back. I'm not proud of it.

steps.goal: Find Caddoc's camp near the old tomb in the eastern hills

clue.name: a cold campfire and a bedroll

steps.text: The fire is days cold. His bedroll is still here, and beside it, scratched into a stone: 'Gone below. Back by dark.' He never came back for the bedroll.

steps.goal: Go into the Tomb of Mithra and look for anyone who saw him
steps.say:
A young man with a lantern? Yes. He went past me singing, if you can believe it. I warned him the deeper halls belong to the cult - the ones who still keep Mithra's rites over the dead. He laughed and said he'd be quick.

That was four days ago. If you go after him, look where they bring their [offerings].

steps.goal: Search the cult's offering halls deep in the tomb
steps.text: Caddoc's lantern, dented and dark. The map is folded inside it, and on the back, in a shaking hand: 'They are not dead. They are not dead. They want me to stay.'
As he falls, the thing that was Caddoc Hale stills. For a heartbeat his eyes are his own. 'Tell Maren,' he whispers, 'I'm sorry. Tell her I found something after all.'

stages.name: The Unquiet Offering
stages.announce: Something shambles out of the dark with a familiar face. The cult's whispering rises: another offering, another servant.
stages.fail: You fall back into the tunnels.

steps.goal: Return to Maren Hale in Cotswold
steps.text: Maren sees your face before you say a word.

steps.say:
You found him. I can see it. Don't - just tell me. Was it quick? Is he... is he coming home?

You could tell her [the truth]. Or you could [spare her], and tell her he went south to find work.

options.say:
...Raised. By those things. And you gave him rest.

Then he isn't down there in the dark any more. That's - that's something. Thank you for not lying to me. I think I'd have known.

South? To work? Caddoc?

Then he's alive. He's alive and he's a fool, and one day he'll walk through that door with a story. I'll keep his supper warm. Thank you. Thank you.

truth.text: Our father's ring was meant to go to Caddoc. He'd want it to go to someone brave. And his lantern - keep that too. He'd like it being carried somewhere.

mercy.text: Here - for your trouble. It's not much. When he comes back, I'll tell him who to thank.

quests.title: The Pilgrim's Letters
quests.offer:
My son Elric went north with a band of pilgrims a month ago. Holy men, he said - dwarves, of all things, from some deep hall. His first letters were full of hymns. The last one... the last one called me 'the woman who raised me' and told me to burn my [loom].

I'm a weaver. I don't know how to go and fetch a boy back from a faith. But you might. Will you [find him]?

topics.loom: His father built it. Elric used to sleep under it when he was small. Now he writes that it's 'a chain of the world above'. He's twenty. He doesn't know what a chain is.

quests.summary: Ysolde Marchant's son Elric followed a band of dwarven 'pilgrims' north, and his letters have stopped sounding like him.

steps.goal: Follow the old north road out of Cotswold
steps.text: At the waystone, the road's mud holds a dozen sets of heavy boots - short strides, all in step - and the drag-marks of a cart. Smoke rises from a woodcutter's hut to the east.

steps.goal: Ask the woodcutter about the pilgrims
steps.say:
Pilgrims? Is that what they call themselves? Short fellows in grey, aye, and a lot of tall young folk walking with them like sleepwalkers. They camp up the hill by the old stones and they sing till dawn. Same three notes. My dog won't go near.

The young ones throw away everything they brought - I've found purses, boots, [letters] in the bracken.

steps.goal: Search the bracken below the pilgrims' camp
steps.text: Letters, dozens of them, never sent. One in Elric's hand, half-finished: 'Mother - I can't remember the colour of the loom. The Brothers say that's good. Why does it feel like drowning?'

steps.goal: Bring Elric back to himself - and out of the camp
steps.text: Elric stares at the letter in his own hand for a long time. Then he asks, very quietly, whether the loom is still there.

stages.name: Three Notes
stages.objective: Keep Elric alive while he wakes
stages.announce: You read Elric his own words. He blinks - and the singing stops. Every grey robe turns towards him.
stages.thanks: I... I know you. No. I know the letter. Who are you?
stages.fail: Elric is dragged back into the singing.

stages.name: The Deep Hall's Voice
stages.objective: Silence the priest who leads the singing
stages.announce: A dwarf in grey steps out of the stones, still humming the three notes. 'The boy is ours. The world above is a lie. Come below.'

boss.name: Brother Thrangar of the Deep Hall

stages.fail: The hymn swells and you are driven off the hill.

steps.goal: Bring word to Ysolde in Cotswold
steps.text: Elric took the long way home - through every field he used to play in, he said. He's there before you.

steps.say: He walked in and sat down under the loom like he was six years old. He hasn't said much. He keeps touching the threads.

home.text: His father made this loom. I'd like you to have something from it - I wove this the night you left, hoping. Take whichever suits you.

quests.title: The Bell-Wether's Price
quests.offer:
You're a hero, aren't you? You've got a sword and everything. The faeries took Grandad's silver pipe - the one he plays for the sheep - and now the sheep won't come home and Grandad sits by the fire doing nothing.

They live by the [faerie ring] in the woods north of the lake. Will you [get it back]? I'd do it but I'm eight.

topics.faerie ring: North of the big lake with the lady in it. Don't talk to the lady. Grandad says she's for kings.

quests.summary: Little Tamsin's grandfather's silver pipe was stolen by the faeries north of the lake.

steps.goal: Find the faerie ring north of the lake
steps.text: Tiny laughter all around you, and the tinkle of a dozen stolen bells. Something throws an acorn at your head.
The giggling stops. A faerie in a coat of bluebells drifts down to look at you, clearly unimpressed.

steps.goal: Speak with whoever rules this ring
Bargain with Wren for the silver pipe
steps.say:
You've been terribly rude to my cousins. Still, you came all this way for a little pipe. The Bell-Wether likes it - it plays the sheep-song, and sheep-songs are rare.

I could simply [return] it, since you've proved so tiresome. Or we could [bargain]: let us keep it, and the Bell-Wether will owe you a favour. Faerie favours are worth a great deal more than pipes.

options.say: Oh, very well. Take your pipe. Tell the shepherd his sheep-song is lovely and that he plays it flat.
Wise. Hold out your hand - there. Something to remember us by. The shepherd will find other songs. Probably.

steps.goal: Bring the silver pipe home to Tamsin
steps.say: You got it! You actually got it! Grandad! GRANDAD! Listen - he's playing - and the sheep are coming! Look at them all!

steps.goal: Tell Tamsin what you agreed with the faeries
steps.say:
They're keeping it? For a FAVOUR? That's not fair. That's... that's a grown-up thing to do.

...Grandad says it's all right. He says he'll whittle a new one. He says faeries keep their promises better than most people. I'm still cross.

returned.text: Grandad says to give you this - he says it's for luck, and that you'll need it more than he does now.

bargained.text: ...You can have this. Grandad says. Hmph.
